claims.text: Adding approximately 3 at.% Al to a refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
The Al addition will promote formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale.
A W–Mo–Nb–Ta–V-based refractory high-entropy alloy without deliberate Al forms relatively thick, nonprotective oxides under extreme-temperature oxygen exposure.
Introducing approximately 3 at.% Al during synthesis enables Al segregation and alumina-scale formation at elevated temperature.
The proposed effect is expected during exposure near 1100°C in air or another oxygen-rich atmosphere for approximately 100 hours.
The relevant structural mediator is a thin, continuous, adherent Al2O3 surface layer.
At high temperature, added Al preferentially diffuses to the alloy surface.
Surface Al reacts with oxygen to form a dense, slow-growing Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale limits oxygen ingress and thereby reduces internal oxidation and alloy degradation.
Compared with the untreated alloy, the Al-modified alloy will show markedly lower oxidation-associated weight gain.
Compared with the untreated alloy, the Al-modified alloy will form a thinner and more adherent oxide scale.
Compared with the untreated alloy, the Al-modified alloy will retain greater mechanical integrity during high-temperature exposure.
Under identical test conditions, the Al-free baseline forms a thicker, less adherent oxide layer that leads to accelerated degradation.
The predicted benefit depends on having enough Al to form a continuous alumina layer.
The predicted benefit also depends on avoiding deleterious effects of Al on high-temperature mechanical properties.
The magnitude of the improvement may depend on interactions with other alloying elements and on processing conditions.
Optimization of Al content may be required to balance oxidation resistance and mechanical performance.
Failure of the Al-modified alloy to show a statistically significant reduction in weight gain and improved scale characteristics relative to the Al-free control would reject the hypothesis.
